ALGORITHM ANXIETY ◆ CREATOR ECONOMY ◆ SOCIAL MEDIA THEATER ◆ CHRONICALLY ONLINE ◆ ARTIFICIAL AUTHENTICITY

01 / The premise

Clothes for people who can see the machinery.

Low Value Content turns the rituals of online life into concise, wearable observations. The target is the system—the engagement bait, professional performance, compulsive refreshing, and monetized sincerity—not the person caught inside it.

Every shirt should land in one glance, hold up after the joke, and feel like something you chose to wear rather than something handed out at a conference.

02 / Why a cocktail?

Content Intoxication.

The feed is seductive, excessive, and low in nutritional value. We know that. We keep ordering another round anyway.

The mark

A play button served in an electric cocktail: part warning label, part confession, and fully in on the joke.

THE EDITORIAL TEST

04 / Ten recurring symptoms

The collections.

A hundred working concepts are organized around ten parts of modern life. The first release will stay deliberately small; the catalog gives it somewhere coherent to go next.

01

Social Media Theater

Thought leadership, public performance, and the career journey nobody asked to follow.

02

Algorithm Anxiety

Engagement, recommendation systems, benchmarks, and the need to be computationally noticed.

03

Creator Economy

Personal brands, monetized memories, and content created for people avoiding their lives.

04

Chronically Online

Doomscrolling, notifications, read receipts, and the inconvenient persistence of offline life.

05

Artificial Authenticity

Professionally edited vulnerability, automated relatability, and human-generated errors.

06

Future of Work

Beta coworkers, autonomous supervision, and labor that needs a software update.

07

Productivity Theater

Alignment, calendar identity, status updates, and the operational excellence of looking busy.

08

Performative Sustainability

Renewable outrage, carbon-neutral decks, and values printed beautifully on recycled paper.

09

Terms and Conditions

Subscription lives, premium personalities, free trials, and privacy with ads.

10

Optimized Human

Competitive mindfulness, tracked sleep, recovery routines, and quantified self-care.

05 / Product before merch

The joke is not an excuse for a bad shirt.

01

Wearable first

Neutral, substantial garments and restrained one-color artwork—not disposable novelty blanks.

02

Sample everything

Every offered design and color combination must be reviewed for print, fit, shrinkage, and wash durability.

03

Earn the next drop

The first six concepts test the voice. Only demonstrated demand justifies more products or inventory.
